surface_mechanism_description: The ALD process involves the use of trimethylaluminum (TMA) as the metal precursor and either H2O or O3 as the oxidation precursor. The physical properties of the films were investigated, and it was observed that heating above crystallization enhances electrical properties and thermal stability. The thermal budget promotes silicon diffusion into the Al2O3 film and aluminum diffusion out of the high-k film. The interface layers formed during thermal steps consist of a mixture of different elements, and the presence of hydrogen and carbon was noted, with hydrogen diffusing out at high temperatures.
evidence: The text discusses the ALD process using TMA and either H2O or O3 as oxidation precursors. It mentions the physical properties of the films, the impact of thermal steps on diffusion effects, and the formation of interface layers composed of different elements. The presence of hydrogen and carbon in the films and at the interface is noted, with hydrogen diffusing out at high temperatures. The text also describes the diffusion of silicon and arsenic into the dielectric and aluminum out of the film.
